tldr:
For the original \(p=2\), \(T=3\), exact-spike experiment with known unit noise, the optimal activity-information deficits are first-order sharp over every Borel adaptive policy and every fixed law on the full continuous cube:
\[
 D_A(s)\sim\frac{2}{3\sqrt{6\pi}}\frac{(\log s)^{3/2}}{\sqrt s},
 \qquad
 D_F(s)\sim\frac{1/\sqrt3+\sqrt{3/8}}{3\sqrt{2\pi}}
                 \frac{(\log s)^{3/2}}{\sqrt s}.
\]
The policy-uniform oracle lower bound matches an explicit orthogonal-pilot threshold policy. The exact minimum of the leading fixed Gram objective has diagonal entries three and off-diagonal absolute value one; precisely the binary matrices with that Gram geometry minimize the leading objective. The fixed-to-adaptive deficit ratio is \(1/2+3/(4\sqrt2)>1\). The sharp adaptive construction uses centered single-factor continuations, whereas the leading fixed optimum uses cube vertices. Original-history likelihoods, arbitrary-kernel measurability, selected-branch entropy remainders, scalar constants, and the continuous-cube certificate are proved. This is a prospective causal-activity design benchmark with no claim of superiority at every finite signal level.
gap: Activity-information design is already an established screening objective. Published adaptive-sensing guarantees and covariance-subspace classification results do not determine the exact first Shannon deficit in this repeatable three-action experiment, or its globally optimized fixed comparator.
fill: A sharp comparison requires an attainable policy and a matching converse against every admissible policy, an activity-specific full-cube fixed certificate, and quantified weak-effect and degenerate-design controls. These are the combined deliverables of Open-ended Question sharp comparison.
